newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up on local buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up on local buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Thursday on heavy buying by local buyers who took long-term positions, brokers said.
The all share index closed 9.6 points up at 869.7, with price gains outnumbering declines by 56 to 17. Bata rose 2.25 rupees to 27.25 and Aitken Spence five rupees to 225.
"There was heavy local buying as investors bought stocks expecting better second half earnings," said a trader at brokerage John Keells.
Colombo stocks have gained over 70 points in July on the back of good interim results for the period ending June 31.
Turnover was 121.8 million rupees, led by local buying. Foreign buying, which was limited to blue chips, amounted to 24.43 million rupees and selling was 38.5 million rupees.
The Colombo Stock Exchange imposed a one-day trading ban on Thursday on shares of Vanik Incorporation Ltd and Forbes Ceylon Ltd to disseminate news about a proposed merger.
Vanik said in a letter to the CSE it was negotiating with Global Equity Corporation to buy the Canadian firm's 50 percent stake in Forbes Ceylon on a general offer.
